claim: The Regulation governs differentiated objects including AI systems, GPAI models, high-risk systems, certain practices, and specified risks/interests.
direct_evidence: Article 1(2) lists rules for AI systems and GPAI models; Articles 5–7 define prohibited practices and high-risk classification; Article 3 defines AI system and risk.
inferential_step: Object categories are extracted from the Regulation's express subject matter, definitions and classification provisions.

claim: The Regulation identifies covered operator/affected-person categories and limits its personal and material scope.
direct_evidence: Article 2(1) enumerates providers, deployers, importers, distributors, product manufacturers, authorised representatives and affected persons; Article 2(3)–(12) states exclusions and qualifications.
inferential_step: The legal list and exclusions define the formal scope of actors and governed conduct.

claim: For high-risk systems, provider duties include risk management, data governance, documentation, logs, transparency/oversight design and post-market monitoring.
direct_evidence: Article 9(1) requires a risk-management system; Article 10(2) requires data governance practices; Article 11(1) requires technical documentation; Article 12 requires logging; Article 72(1) requires provider post-market monitoring.
inferential_step: Multiple express assignments are grouped by the lifecycle governance functions they support.

claim: Deployers have separate high-risk-system use and human-oversight obligations.
direct_evidence: Article 26(1) requires appropriate measures to use systems according to instructions; Article 26(2) requires assignment of human oversight to competent, trained and authorized persons.
inferential_step: The provision expressly assigns conduct to deployers and connects use to provider instructions.

claim: Third-party conformity assessment is part of defined routes, while Article 43 does not make notified-body involvement universal.
direct_evidence: Article 3(21) defines conformity-assessment bodies as performing third-party assessment; Article 43(1) allows internal control or a notified-body route in the stated circumstances.
inferential_step: The text creates a conditional provider-to-assessment-body relation; route conditions preclude generalizing it to every high-risk system.

claim: Providers' cooperation/reporting duties connect to Member State market surveillance, which has evaluation and corrective powers; Union safeguard review is specified.
direct_evidence: Article 21 requires information on reasoned request; Article 73 requires serious-incident reporting; Article 79 authorizes national evaluation and measures; Article 81 specifies Commission evaluation of certain national measures.
inferential_step: Cross-provision links establish a provider-authority information/enforcement relation and national-to-Union safeguard relation.

claim: Designated fundamental-rights bodies may access specified documentation and must inform the market-surveillance authority of a request.
direct_evidence: Article 77(1) authorizes documentation access where necessary within mandate and requires informing the relevant market-surveillance authority.
inferential_step: The express access and notification duties establish a bounded inter-authority coordination relation, not general supervisory control.

claim: Chapter V assigns exclusive GPAI supervision/enforcement to the Commission, implemented by the AI Office, with specified advisory and provider-facing links.
direct_evidence: Article 88(1) gives the Commission exclusive powers for Chapter V and entrusts implementation to the AI Office; Articles 90–93 specify alert, information, evaluation and measures.
inferential_step: Cross-provision coding groups the Chapter V powers and stated links as a distinct subject-matter pathway.

claim: Member States designate notifying authorities to assess, designate, notify and monitor conformity-assessment bodies.
direct_evidence: Article 28(1) assigns each Member State designation/establishment of at least one notifying authority for the stated procedures and monitoring.
inferential_step: The express assignment constitutes national authority over entry and oversight of assessment bodies.

claim: Public authority is allocated by function across Member State and Union actors, including a distinct Commission Chapter V remit.
direct_evidence: Articles 79–84 give Member State market-surveillance authorities evaluation and corrective functions; Article 81 gives the Commission a safeguard decision role; Article 88(1) specifies exclusive Commission powers for Chapter V.
inferential_step: Authority is compared across statutory functions and objects; no actor's remit is generalized beyond its text.

claim: Legal discretion is bounded and function-specific in provider assessment-route choice, deployer resource organization and public corrective decisions.
direct_evidence: Article 26(3) preserves deployer freedom to organize resources for oversight; Article 43 conditions route choice; Articles 79–84 authorize measures within specified tests and procedures.
inferential_step: Express choice and evaluative standards are coded as scoped discretion, not inferred from institutional status.

claim: Information duties support oversight, while explicit hearing, judicial review and procedural safeguards provide more complete accountability features.
direct_evidence: Articles 21 and 73 provide authority-facing information; Article 101(2) provides an opportunity to be heard and Article 101(5) gives the Court of Justice unlimited jurisdiction to review fines; Article 99(10) requires procedural safeguards and judicial remedies.
inferential_step: Information is distinguished from answerability, assessment and consequence; only the latter combined features support the accountability characterization.

claim: The Regulation constitutes a differentiated, hybrid, multilevel formal governance architecture for the matters within its legal scope.
direct_evidence: The text assigns operator-side lifecycle duties, deployer duties, conditional external assessment, national surveillance and Union safeguard roles, and a distinct Commission-centered Chapter V pathway.
inferential_step: Linked configurations with distinct objects, functions, authorities and constraints support a bounded architectural inference; the claim is not based on frequency and is limited to formal design.

claim: No unified regime boundary or all-purpose single governance logic is assigned to the Regulation on this evidence.
legal_anchors: Articles 1–113; V8 regime boundary and stopping principles
direct_evidence: The Regulation contains differentiated pathways and cross-references but does not establish that its text exhausts wider institutional arrangements.
inferential_step: V8 requires regime boundaries to be inferred from broader institutional evidence and architecture claims to stop at the highest supported level.
